seo.title: SSH tunnels, cloud sign-in and connection import
seo.description: Reach databases through SSH jump hosts, proxies or kubectl, sign in with AWS IAM or Entra ID, and bring connections over from TablePlus, DBeaver and more.

header.title: Connections
header.lead: Save and organize connections, reach private servers through SSH and sign in with supported cloud accounts.

sections.title: Organize connections
paragraphs: Fill connection settings from a URL, including jdbc: and +ssh URLs. Use Use clipboard URL to import one you copied.
Arrange connections in nested groups, add tags and colors, and mark favorites. Try the bundled SQLite sample with <ui>Open Sample Database</ui>.
Keep multiple connections in one window or use <ui>Open in New Window</ui>. Each connection remembers its last tab.

sections.title: Import connections
paragraphs: Import from another database client, project configuration files or your AWS account.

blocks.title: From another database client
paragraphs: Import from Other App reads {connectionImportApps}, including TablePlus's Setapp edition. Password import depends on how the source app stores them. DBeaver and Navicat encrypted passwords are supported; Navicat requires an .ncx export.

blocks.title: From a project’s config files
paragraphs: <ui>Open Project Folder</ui> finds database settings in supported environment, framework and Docker configuration files. Review each source before importing; passwords go to the Keychain. Recognized production names start at Alert rather than the usual Safe Mode default.

blocks.title: From your AWS account
paragraphs: Import from AWS lists the RDS instances and Aurora clusters an AWS profile can see in the regions you pick, and adds the ones you choose. The profile needs rds:DescribeDBInstances and rds:DescribeDBClusters.

blocks.title: SSH and TLS
paragraphs: Connect over SSH with passwords, keys, agents or interactive prompts. Use jump hosts or ProxyJump, and reuse tunnels as SSH profiles. Unknown host keys require fingerprint approval.
Choose TLS mode and provide CA or client certificates. Required encrypts without validating the server certificate; Verify CA and Verify Identity add certificate checks.

engines.label: Network engines without an SSH tunnel

blocks.title: Proxies, Cloudflare, Cloud SQL and tunnel commands
paragraphs: Use SOCKS5 with remote DNS or Cloudflare Access through cloudflared. For {cloudSqlProxy}, TablePro downloads, verifies and runs the Cloud SQL Auth Proxy.
Tunnel Command connects through a local port opened by kubectl port-forward, aws ssm start-session or your own command. Pre-connect shell scripts ask for approval each session.

sections.title: Sign in with your cloud account
paragraphs: AWS IAM database authentication signs a fresh token at every connect, from an access key, a profile in ~/.aws (with credential_process and assumed roles) or AWS IAM Identity Center. It also turns TLS up to Required. Amazon ElastiCache for Redis, Amazon Keyspaces and DynamoDB have their own AWS signing.

SQL Server signs in with Microsoft Entra ID in the browser, using the client ID of an app registration you provide, or with Kerberos from a ticket or a principal and password. Google BigQuery takes a service account key, Application Default Credentials or Google OAuth with your own client, and Google Cloud Spanner and the Cloud SQL Auth Proxy can use your Google account.

engines.label: AWS IAM authentication on RDS and Aurora

sections.title: Credentials and password sources
paragraphs: Passwords and SSH-key passphrases are stored in the macOS Keychain. Password sync through iCloud Keychain is a separate opt-in setting. SSH key files stay on disk.

Free credential profiles reuse logins and read passwords from 1Password, Vault, AWS Secrets Manager, commands, files or environment variables. Required CLI tools must be installed. Sources never sync. PostgreSQL-family connections can also use ~/.pgpass where supported.

blocks.title: Environment Variables
paragraphs: Use references such as $DB_HOST in supported connection fields. Values come from the app's environment at connect time. Port and password fields are excluded; passwords use separate, free sources.

sections.title: Connection policies
paragraphs: Safe Mode controls statement confirmation. External Clients controls MCP and AppleScript access, defaults to Read Only and stays on this Mac. The AI policy controls assistant access; Never also blocks MCP clients.
An organization can enforce a minimum Safe Mode level for every connection, and control updates, through a configuration profile.

blocks.title: Connect and query timeouts
paragraphs: Each connection can set its own connect timeout, which covers the network, TLS, sign-in and any tunnel or proxy, and its own query timeout in place of the app-wide one. The query timeout applies to the drivers that support one, after you reconnect.

sections.title: On iPhone and iPad
paragraphs: The iPhone and iPad app has its own connection form for {iosPicker}, with groups, one tag per connection and favorites. SSH tunnels sign in with a password or a private key, from a file or pasted in, and check the host key; SSH agents and jump hosts are not supported on iPhone and iPad. TLS can verify the server’s certificate, except on SQL Server, where it encrypts without verifying. Certificates stay on the device and never sync.

Passwords and pasted keys are kept in the Keychain. SQL Server connections synced from a Mac can sign in with Microsoft Entra ID. Importing from other apps, AWS IAM, Kerberos and Google sign-in, proxies and tunnel commands, password sources and timeouts are in the Mac app only.

availability.label: Minimum Safe Mode level through a configuration profile

limits: Password sources and the Network tab’s proxies and tunnel commands stay on the Mac where you set them: they never sync, so a synced connection needs them set up again on each Mac.

TablePro reads the environment it was started with. Opened from the Dock or Finder, it does not see the variables your shell profile sets, which affects the environment-variable password source and Environment Variables alike.
When a plan ends, $DB_HOST and other references are no longer filled in and reach the server as typed, with no warning.
Open Project Folder is a one-time import: nothing is watched, and importing the same settings twice creates two connections.
AWS IAM authentication covers {awsIam}, not Amazon Redshift. A configuration profile can enforce a minimum Safe Mode level and update settings, nothing more.
